A.strength: skills block up top (C++17, Linux, CMake) and a Robotics Experience heading make fit obvious in seconds
A.weakness: legged project cut to two bullets, losing the verification depth; Emerson manufacturing filler; PyTorch not listed

B.strength: focused robotics-software summary plus the full EKF verification story (finite-difference Jacobians, 1e-13 match to Python, observability)
B.weakness: gimmicky bullet labels ('Proved it before trusting it') and skills left at the bottom

C.strength: results-first bullets with crisp quantified outcomes (100x RMSE, 46%, 58%)
C.weakness: outcome-first wording over-credits team results (4.7% material, 31->87% decoding), uses first-person 'I', and drops the observability/reference checks

D.strength: deepest Boston Dynamics content (delta-v metric validated against synthetic pulses) with a skills-first layout naming C++17, Linux and physics simulation
D.weakness: keyword-heavy skills block, and calling a simulated estimator's update 'real-time'

E.strength: says clearly what ran on the real robot vs in simulation, and states Summer 2027 availability
E.weakness: mechanical/manufacturing filler (Emerson, CATIA fixtures, CNC/GD&T) weakens the software fit and pushes the C++ work below the fold

F.strength: Boston Dynamics Atlas co-op shown up front
F.weakness: C++ EKF project buried in one vague bullet, no portfolio/code link, CAD-heavy skills, no C++17 or PyTorch, hobbies padding

G.strength: complete, clean C++ EKF/control project with verification and closed-loop metrics (0.004 m/s vs ground truth, QP 0.169->0.091), sim clearly labeled
G.weakness: no summary and skills only at the bottom, so the recruiter scan is slower

notes: The top versions put the C++17/Linux skills and the simulation-based robotics work up front, and kept the evidence that the EKF was verified (finite-difference Jacobians, a Python reference match, observability analysis). The bottom versions read like a mechanical/manufacturing resume (Emerson, CATIA fixtures, CAD-heavy skills) and buried or watered down the C++ project; F also drops the code link. No version shows CUDA, ROS or OpenGL, or an EE/CE degree, which caps every score.
